# Introduction

For my first dataset, I selected life expectancy data from the World Bank. I want to explore how life expectancy changed across different countries before, during, and after the COVID-19 pandemic. I am particularly interested in understanding whether countries recovered at the same rate or whether some countries continued to experience lower life expectancy.

# Data Source

The dataset comes from the World Bank's World Development Indicators database.

- **Dataset:** Life expectancy at birth, total (years)
- **Indicator:** SP.DYN.LE00.IN
- **Source:** [World Bank Life Expectancy Data](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/SP.DYN.LE00.IN)

The original dataset contains countries, regional aggregates, and separate columns for each year. I also downloaded the country metadata and indicator information to help interpret the data.

# Research Question

How did life expectancy change between 2019 and 2024, and which countries experienced the strongest and weakest recoveries following the COVID-19 pandemic?

# Data Tidying Approach

The original dataset is in wide format because each year is stored in a separate column. I plan to use `pivot_longer()` from the `tidyr` package to convert the year columns into two variables: `Year` and `LifeExpectancy`.

I will also use `dplyr` to select relevant variables, identify missing values, and separate individual countries from regional aggregates using the World Bank country metadata. I will keep the original CSV unchanged and perform all transformations in R.

# Planned Analysis

I plan to compare life expectancy in 2019, 2021, and 2024 to examine the decline and recovery around the pandemic. I will calculate changes in life expectancy for individual countries and compare patterns across regions and income groups.

I also plan to create line charts showing trends over time and bar charts highlighting countries with the largest declines and recoveries.

# Expected Challenges

Some countries may have missing observations, especially for recent years. The dataset also includes regional and income-group aggregates, which need to be distinguished from individual countries. Additionally, changes during the pandemic cannot automatically be attributed entirely to COVID-19.

# Expected Outcome

I hope to identify differences in life expectancy recovery across countries and regions and better understand how global health outcomes changed during and after the pandemic.
